Well, I, uh... I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to stop doing the same things over and over again, every single day. It’s like my whole life is just consumed by it, you know? Yeah, all the time. It's exactly like that, actually. I'll be sitting there, maybe just trying to eat dinner or watch a show, and I know I did a job right earlier in the day. I know my way around tools, you know, so if I fix a socket or hang something up, I know I did it properly. But then... it's like my brain just turns on me. I'll suddenly start thinking that there's a loose wire I missed behind the wallplate. I'll convince myself I left a nail somewhere on the floor. And the thing is, I try so hard to ignore it. I really do. I'll sit there gripping the arms of my chair, telling myself to just think about the TV, think about anything else, because I know I swept the floor. I know I tightened the wire. But I try to push those thoughts out, and they just... they come right back stronger. It's like arguing with a brick wall. The harder I try not to think about the house burning down or my wife bleeding, the louder the thoughts get, until it's literally all I can see in my head and I'm practically sweating. It just loops and loops and loops until I finally give up and go get a flashlight to check the floorboards again.

Well, yeah, exactly. Like I was trying to explain earlier when I said I spend most of my day going back over the same things... it's not just a quick glance. It’s... it's a whole ordeal. It has to be done a very specific way or it doesn't count.

I have to push on the door with my shoulder, twist the knob, maybe three or four times, and then run my thumb over the deadbolt to feel that it's flush. And my tools—if I'm checking my tools, they have to be perfectly straight. If a wrench is slightly angled, or if I spot a tiny speck of dust on the workbench after I just wiped it... I have to take everything off the bench, wipe the dust down all over again, and put them all back exactly right. 

I'll just keep checking and fixing them, again and again. Lining them up, wiping the dust, testing the outlets, pushing on the doors... I do it for hours. I literally do it until my knees hurt and I'm just completely worn out. My hands will be dry from wiping things down, my back will be aching, and I'll just be physically drained. But the crazy thing is—and this is what's driving me out of my mind—even after doing it perfectly, exactly the way my brain demands, I still don't feel sure. I just never feel sure enough to leave it alone. I'll be standing there, totally exhausted, and I'll still think, "Wait, did I actually push the plug all the way in, or did I just imagine doing it?" And because I can't be one hundred percent certain, I have to start the whole routine over again.

Yeah, definitely. Especially with my tools, like I was saying. It’s... it’s not just about them being there, it’s about how they are there, if that makes sense. Like, if I’m looking at my wrenches, they can’t just be in the drawer. They have to be perfectly lined up, from smallest to largest, and the gaps between them have to be exactly the same. If one is slightly askew, or if the handles aren't perfectly parallel... it just feels completely wrong. It’s like this itch in my brain that I can’t scratch until it’s fixed. 

And it’s the same with the dust, too. When I’m wiping down the workbench or the shelves, I have to wipe in straight lines. I can’t just do circles or a quick swipe. It has to be methodical, perfectly even strokes, overlapping just right. If I miss a spot, or if the rag leaves a streak that breaks the pattern, I have to start the whole surface over again. 

That’s what I mean when I say I spend most of my day going back over the same outlets, locks, tools, and dust in the house. I’m just checking and fixing them again and again, trying to get that perfect order, that perfect symmetry, because if it’s not perfect, it’s not safe. It’s not done. I’ll stand there for hours, lining up the screwdrivers, wiping the bench, adjusting the pliers, over and over until my hands ache and my back is killing me. I do it until I’m completely worn out, but even then... even when it looks perfectly straight to anyone else, I still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone. I’ll look at it and think, "Is that wrench a millimeter off?" And then I have to fix it again. It's exhausting, doc. Just totally exhausting.

Oh, absolutely. The order is... well, it’s everything. If I don’t do it in the exact right sequence, the whole thing feels ruined and I have to start all over from the very beginning. I can’t just randomly check a lock and then wander over to an outlet. No, it has to follow a strict path. I'm just checking and fixing them, again and again, trying to get the order perfectly right without any interruptions or mistakes. I'll do the whole circuit until my legs are shaking and I’m completely worn out, just physically and mentally drained. But even then, even after doing the whole routine in the exact right order, I'll get to the end and my brain will say, 'Wait, did you do the hallway outlet before or after the bathroom?' And because of that one tiny piece of doubt, I still don’t feel sure enough to leave it alone. I can't just walk away. So I go back to the bedroom. I start the whole sequence over. It just eats up my entire day.

That’s... wow, that’s a really tough question to wrap my head around. Because, honestly, I can’t even imagine my brain working that way anymore. If I didn't have that terrifying image of the house burning down or my wife stepping on a rusty nail... would I still do it?

I mean... I feel like we keep circling back to this, Doc. If I could be absolutely, one hundred percent certain? Yeah, maybe I'd stop. But that's just it—that certainty you're talking about, it just doesn't exist for me. It's like a phantom.

That doubt just never, ever goes away. It doesn't matter how many times I look at the deadbolt, it doesn't matter if I jiggled the handle fifty times. The feeling of 'what if' is still right there in my chest. So, sure, if I could somehow just magically *know* nothing bad would happen, maybe I could finally rest and stop worrying about the house. But my brain won't let me get to that point of certainty. I just keep checking until I'm totally worn out, and even then, it never feels like enough to just walk away.

Foreign. Absolutely, one hundred percent foreign. I mean, I know I keep bringing up the same exact examples, doc, but it’s because it just doesn't make any sense to me. Well, it's definitely not a habit, Doc. I mean, who would have a habit of making themselves miserable? A habit is like... I don't know, drinking a cup of coffee every morning at seven, or always putting your left shoe on before your right. It's something you do without thinking, right? But this... this is all I think about. It's totally driven by fear. That anxiety, that absolute dread that something terrible is going to happen if I don't do it. 

And I know I'm repeating myself, I know I keep saying the same things over and over to you today, but it's just the absolute truth of my life right now. I'm here, sitting in this office, because I literally spend most of my day going back over the exact same things. Over and over. The outlets in the living room, the locks on the front and back doors, the tools out in the garage, making sure they're perfectly put away so nobody gets hurt... even the dust in the house.
